title: The OR Sound
kidRule: O and R team up to say 'or', like in ORBIT. At the end of a word the sound is often spelled O-R-E with a quiet E, like in IGNORE. A few words use other spellings, like DOOR and FOUR.
hint: Listen for the 'or' sound. Is it in the middle of the word or right at the very end? That is a clue for how to spell it.
reminder: The 'or' sound has two main spellings: O-R, and O-R-E with a quiet E at the end of a word. If one did not work, try the other one!

check.question: Why is there a quiet E at the end of IGNORE?
check.correctAnswer: Because the 'or' sound at the end of a word is often spelled O-R-E!
distractors: Because the E says 'ee' at the end of the word
Because words are never allowed to end in the letter R

words.def: The curved path that something in space follows around a planet or a star.
words.sent: The moon travels in an orbit around the Earth.
words.story: The International Space Station zips around the Earth about 16 times every day, so the astronauts on board see 16 sunrises!
words.card: My dog chased his tail in *orbit* until he was a *bit* dizzy!

words.def: To pay no attention to someone or something.
words.sent: I try to ignore my brother when he makes silly faces.
words.story: Cats can recognize their own names, but scientists found that they often just choose to ignore us!
words.card: Neither the cat *nor* the goldfish could *ignore* the dancing broccoli!

words.def: The place where two walls, sides, or streets meet.
words.sent: The cat sleeps in the corner of my room.
words.story: A triangle has three corners and a square has four, but a circle has no corners at all!
words.card: A mouse nibbled *corn* on the cob in the *corner* of the kitchen!

words.def: The small nut of an oak tree, which sits in a little cup.
words.sent: The squirrel hid an acorn under the leaves.
words.story: One big oak tree can drop thousands of acorns in a single year!
words.card: The squirrel planted an *acorn* and hoped it would grow pop*corn*!

words.def: To love someone or something very, very much.
words.sent: My grandparents adore their fluffy old cat.
words.story: Giant pandas adore bamboo so much that they spend about twelve hours a day eating it!
words.card: I *do* *adore* a pancake that is taller than my dog!

words.def: To travel around a new place to find out what is there.
words.sent: We love to explore the woods behind our house.
words.story: Robots explore the planet Mars for us! A rover named Perseverance landed there in 2021.
words.card: The brave mole set off to *explore* a cave full of sparkly *ore*!

words.def: A piece of land where fruit trees are grown.
words.sent: We picked apples in the orchard.
words.story: Many orchards keep beehives nearby, because bees carry pollen from blossom to blossom, and that is how the trees can grow fruit!
words.card: It is *hard* to nap in an *orchard* when apples keep bonking your head!

words.def: To soak up a liquid, the way a sponge does.
words.sent: A towel will absorb the spilled milk.
words.story: Sea sponges are animals! They sit on the ocean floor and absorb tiny bits of food from the water that flows through them.
words.card: The wizard's glowing *orb* began to *absorb* all the spilled lemonade!

words.def: Normal and usual, not special or different.
words.sent: It was an ordinary Tuesday until a parrot flew into class.
words.story: An ordinary wooden pencil holds enough graphite to draw a line many miles long!
words.card: An *ordinary* spoon made a mighty *din* when it joined the kitchen band!

words.def: An animal that eats mostly meat.
words.sent: A lion is a carnivore with very sharp teeth.
words.story: The Venus flytrap is a meat eater too, even though it is a plant! It snaps its leaves shut to catch bugs.
words.card: The *carnivore* drove his *car* to the drive-through and ordered ninety meatballs!
